memory.content: render_invoice treats invoice.number == 0 as the "unissued draft" sentinel and renders "INVOICE DRAFT" for it. This relies on the guarantee that no issued invoice can ever have number 0: NEXT_INVOICE starts at 1000 and issue_number() only ever fetch_add's upward, so 0 is reserved exclusively for drafts (Invoice::draft sets number = 0). If the sequence were ever reseeded/wrapped so issue_number() could return 0, an issued invoice would silently render as a draft. Corollary: render_invoice must stay pure — it must never call issue_number() or otherwise consume the global sequence, which was the original bug (previews burned a fresh number and showed a different one each time).
